Technical note: the P_med estimand

Source: vignettes/technical-note-estimand.qmd

Definition

For treatment contrast xx (treated) versus x*x^* (control), mediator MM and outcome YY:

Pmed=P{Y(x,M(x))>Y(x,M(x*))}+12P{Y(x,M(x))=Y(x,M(x*))}.P_{med} = P\{Y(x, M(x)) > Y(x, M(x^*))\} + \tfrac12 P\{Y(x, M(x)) = Y(x, M(x^*))\}.

Treatment is held at xx in both potential outcomes. Only the mediator is varied, and its two draws are independent. This matches Definition 1 of the manuscript and is implemented in .pmed_core_simple() (R/compute-core.R).

Consequences

  • Mediation only. The direct effect c′c' cancels, because xx is the same in both potential outcomes. A test, test-pmed-estimand.R, checks invariance to c′c'.
  • Null value. Pmed=0.5P_{med} = 0.5 when the mediator shift has no effect, so values above 0.5 indicate positive mediation.
  • Ties. The half weight for ties makes the estimand well defined for discrete outcomes.
  • Scale free and bounded. It is a probability, so it lies in [0, 1] regardless of units.

Gaussian closed form

For a Gaussian mediator with path aa, outcome path bb, mediator error SD σm\sigma_m and outcome error SD σy\sigma_y, and a unit treatment contrast,

Pmed=Φ(ab2(b2σm2+σy2)),P_{med} = \Phi\!\left(\frac{a b}{\sqrt{2\,(b^2 \sigma_m^2 + \sigma_y^2)}}\right),

which is about 0.563 at a=b=0.5a = b = 0.5, σm=σy=1\sigma_m = \sigma_y = 1. test-pmed-estimand.R checks the implementation against this formula, checks invariance to c′c', and checks that the indirect effect equals aba b.

Identification

Identification of the mediated shift requires the usual sequential ignorability conditions, including no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding. That assumption is not testable; use sensitivity analysis.

Relation to other estimands

The modern estimands (gauge, incremental, Sobol, Wasserstein, rg-flow) change the scale or the functional, not the identification conditions. See Modern estimands.
